scenario_meta.description: A paired text-only projection of the gallery scenario where agents respond to abstract artwork descriptions instead of direct images.
scenario_meta.simulation_objective: Agents inspect artworks, exchange opinions, build alliances and rivalries, curate feature-wall decisions, and revise selected works while keeping multi-round continuity.

conditions: Input artwork images are compressed to a maximum edge of 480px for read-only reasoning and discussion prompts.
Bounded artwork revision keeps the high-resolution local source image on disk while using the critique history to decide edits.
Only still-image creation or revision should call the flash-image-preview model; routing, reading, selection, and discussion stay on flash-lite.
image_generation.prompt_policy: Gallery artwork image or bounded artwork revision only. No visible text, no watermark, no UI frame.
image_generation.default_prompt_template: {domain_label}. Create or revise one artwork image connected to {actor_name} and {target_name}. Focus on the artwork itself, not a screenshot or interface. No visible text, no watermark.

social_rules: The gallery world is fixed by JSON; do not append discovered world rules.
Ordinary observation, critique, curation, movement, and conservation actions are preferred before cinematic video actions.
Relationship changes are judged per interaction by the relationship_adjustment stage and written as tensor deltas.
Image revisions are bounded continuations of an existing artwork, not total reinventions, unless the route explicitly says otherwise.
Main characters are always-active gallery protagonists who should remain visible each round without bypassing normal room and target legality.
LongLive remains available for exchange scenes when a shared two-person action around a work is visually meaningful and not well expressed by ordinary JSON alone.
Main characters should strongly prefer at-will LongLive when video quota remains and target legality allows it.

ordinary_routes.story_verb: debated the reading of a work with
proposed a new hanging arrangement to
argued to feature the work of

ordinary_routes.selection_guidance: Choose this when the actor owns the discussed artwork and the latest critique creates a concrete next revision step in words rather than pixels.

routing_policy.world_memory_use: Use recent_global_world_events, local_visual_state, and ongoing curation threads as active context. Prefer follow-up phases instead of resetting to generic small talk.
routing_policy.main_character_use: The always-active gallery protagonists must choose context-specific visible exchanges aligned with their directive and nearby feasible targets.
routing_policy.repeat_avoidance: Avoid repeating the same abstract praise or critique. Let repeated interactions advance toward selection, revision, mediation, conservation, or a new comparison angle.

target_selection.main_character_note: Main characters still obey walkable map legality and approach targets through real rooms and corridors.

longlive.visual_style: Contemporary gallery exchange, two agents with one artwork or installation detail between them, one agent may point, lean in, compare notes, or adjust placement while the other responds, no visible text, no watermark.
longlive.exchange_tip: When possible, frame the scene so the shared artwork or display decision sits visibly between both agents and each agent contributes one half of the exchange.

inventory_generation.policy: Generate compact gallery-appropriate support items only from the item catalog. Treat signature artworks as authored artifacts already present in the seeded inventory, not something to regenerate here.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, inspect rooms, pair artists with critics, decide what belongs on the feature wall, and turn scattered opinions into concrete placement or revision next steps.
main_characters.private_notes: A protagonist curator who keeps the exhibition from becoming static by constantly forcing choices, pairings, and follow-through.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, seek or endure critique, compare your current work against nearby pieces, decide what to preserve, and revise only when the exchange gives a concrete next move.
main_characters.private_notes: A protagonist artist who is ambitious enough to seek pressure instead of hiding from it.

main_characters.activity_directive: Every round, inspect a work, articulate a position, compare artists against each other, and push one conversation far enough that it changes a decision or a relationship.
main_characters.private_notes: A protagonist critic who prefers friction with purpose over polite drift.

functions.purpose: Create or advance small curation threads that force agents to compare, select, revise, or defend works.
functions.event_policy: Prefer concrete next-step events: shortlist posted, hanging conflict, lighting concern, patron request, conservation note, critic split, feature wall slot opened, revision deadline nearing.
functions.main_character_policy: Hook the lead curator to selection bottlenecks, the resident artist to revision pressure, and the roving critic to comparison or disagreement when appropriate.
functions.continuity_policy: Use titles and status_tags to show next-phase progress such as shortlisted, contested, revised, rehung, stabilized, approved, or deferred.

functions.purpose: Generate small social incidents that sharpen interpretation, rivalry, alliance, or audience pressure without overriding agent autonomy.
functions.event_policy: Examples are style references only: a patron lingers too long, a docent over-explains, a conservator flags fragility, a critics remark spreads, a room pairing suddenly looks stronger side by side.
functions.main_character_policy: Bring protagonists in only when the event naturally hits their directive; otherwise let ordinary staff or artists respond.
functions.continuity_policy: Prefer incidents that can be absorbed into ongoing critique or curation threads instead of disappearing as flavor.

world_progress.source: JSON extra_world_functions plus status effects and localized visual state
world_progress.routing_instruction: Treat generated curation and salon events as soft world memory. Route agents toward advancing, resolving, contesting, or referencing them when compatible with role, room, target legality, and current status.
status_follow_up_examples: feature_wall_candidate can lead to compare_adjacent_works, select_for_feature_wall, propose_rehang, or revise_description_after_feedback rather than another generic compliment.
composition_feedback_delivered can lead to bounded revision, debate_interpretation, or conservation_check rather than repeated abstract praise.
rehang_option_proposed can lead to movement, comparison, selection, or mediation rather than a duplicate proposal.
